scope: United States Consumer Expenditure Survey 2024 distribution baseline
purpose: Establish an official BLS population-distribution baseline for Physical Economics so national aggregates are not treated as sufficient when expenditure capacity and burden differ materially by income quintile.
source_authority: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Expenditure Surveys

construction.quintile_method: BLS sorts consumer units from lowest to highest income before taxes, applies population weights, and divides the weighted population into five equal parts.

derived_distribution_metrics.interpretation: The national average cannot represent a typical burden state for every income stratum because expenditure capacity differs by more than fourfold between the highest and lowest weighted income quintiles.

bounded_findings: A national expenditure average materially compresses the population distribution: 2024 average annual expenditures were $35,046 in the lowest income quintile and $150,342 in the highest.

Food, housing, and transportation together represented 63.3 percent of average 2024 expenditures across all consumer units, making essential or near-essential categories structurally dominant in the household expenditure surface.
This baseline establishes why Physical Economics must calculate burden by population strata before national aggregation.
These 2024 levels are a distributional baseline, not a claim that 2026 household burdens are identical; current HTOPS and later CE data must update the state.
